subject: Telemetry sidecar coop pilot — cost-share & technical healthcheck
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Alvarez <maria@observify.io>, alliances@datadog.com, integrations@grafana.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Telemetry sidecar coop pilot — cost-share & technical healthcheck

Hi Maria + Datadog/Grafana alliances teams —

Thanks for the productive sync last week. We ran the environment smoke tests on our side and think there's a clear path to run a focused pilot that validates: trace continuity from inference requests, prefix-based metrics deduping, and low-overhead collection with an OpenTelemetry sidecar.

Proposed scope (3 weeks):
- Week 0: technical healthcheck (sampling plan, network egress, retention constraints)
- Week 1: sidecar deployment (OTel Collector config) to a single Redwood Dedicated pool
- Week 2: integration of traces into Datadog + Prometheus metrics surfaced to Grafana dashboards, end-to-end verification with latency-sensitive load tests

Operational asks:
- Observify: installation + config of collector and small adapter layer for request attribution
- Datadog: short checklist for agent compatibility (OTLP over gRPC, APM tagging guidance)
- Grafana: template dashboard and Prometheus metrics naming guidance to avoid high cardinality

Budget idea: Redwood covers infra + orchestration (40%), Observify contributes integration engineering (30%), Datadog/Grafana provide tooling credits or support hours (30%). We can be flexible on splits but want clarity before we spin up dedicated test GPUs.

I attached a draft pilot-scope.pdf and a starting otelcol-config.yaml for review.

Next steps: please confirm technical blockers and any legal/data controls (e.g., where traces can be stored, PII filtering) by EOD tomorrow so we can lock the timeline.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Director, Partnerships | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
Attachment: pilot-scope.pdf (application/pdf)
Attachment: otelcol-config.yaml (text/plain)
From: Maria Alvarez <maria@observify.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: alliances@datadog.com, integrations@grafana.com, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 14:10:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Telemetry sidecar coop pilot — cost-share & technical healthcheck

Ben — thanks, sounds promising. Observify can take on the collector deployment and the small adapter to map Redwood request IDs into the trace/span attributes. A few clarifying Qs before we sign off on the plan: 

1) Data residency: will traces and metrics be forwarded out of the customer VPC to Datadog/Grafana cloud? If so, we need to document egress rules and encryption (TLS + mTLS).
2) Sampling: for latency-sensitive inference paths we prefer adaptive sampling at the collector to avoid token-level overhead. Does Redwood runtime emit a stable request_id header we can key on?
3) Cardinality cap: we'll need a cap parameter in the collector config to limit label explosion (we can default to 100 unique tags per metric).

If those are OK, Observify will schedule a 2-day install window during Week 1 and provide a short runbook.

—Maria
Maria Alvarez
Engineering Lead, Integrations | Observify
maria@observify.io

Date: Fri, 23 Oct 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Telemetry sidecar coop pilot — cost-share & technical healthcheck

Thanks Maria — quick technical answers and a proposed mutual action plan attached.

Short answers:
- Data residency: pilot will forward OTLP over TLS to partner endpoints; we will not persist raw request payloads. We'll redact prompt content at the agent level and only keep trace metadata per the attached policy doc.
- Request ID: yes — Redwood runtime sets X-Redwood-Request-Id (stable for retries) and we can map that into trace attributes.
- Cardinality: agreed on default cap at 100 unique label values; we will add an enforcement hook in the collector pipeline to drop high-cardinality labels and record a metric when it happens.

Mutual action plan (brief):
- Week 0 (healthcheck): legal + security sign-off on data flows, collect endpoint details, agree sampling budget (we suggest 2% head sampling + adaptive 10% on errors)
- Week 1 (deploy): Observify deploys collector, Redwood provides sample load test harness, Datadog/Grafana validate ingestion and recommended templates
- Week 2 (verify): joint smoke tests, dashboard handoff, runbook sign-off, after-action notes and a go/no-go decision on production rollout

Attachments included: pilot-scope.pdf, otelcol-config.yaml, and a short security-notes.pdf (redaction + retention). Please review the security notes carefully — security needs explicit confirmation on retention windows.

PO / commercial ask: If everyone is aligned, procurement will need a small MSA amendment and a PO from Observify to cover their engineering days. I put a provisional PO number in the HubSpot deal but will wait for formal PO.

Laura Bennett
Partner Program Manager | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Attachments: pilot-scope.pdf (application/pdf), otelcol-config.yaml (text/plain), security-notes.pdf (application/pdf)

Thanks all — security has reviewed the security-notes.pdf and is OK with the redaction approach and a 30-day retention window for derived traces. They've asked for an audit hook (export of access logs) which we can provide.

I confirmed two days of field SE time (me + one engineer) for Week 1 and reserved a small Dedicated pool for the load tests. I also linked the HubSpot deal here: https://hubspot.redwood.ai/deals/DEAL-3589 — please add PO/contract items there.
